title: H 3594 (South Carolina Constitutional Carry/Second Amendment Preservation Act of 2023), Act No. 111 (R121) (125th Session, 2023-2024) — Constitutional carry: handgun carry is unlawful only in listed places; plus penalties, permit changes, expungement and training
operative_text:
Sec. 1 short title: This act may be cited as the "South Carolina Constitutional Carry/Second Amendment Preservation Act of 2023."
Sec. 2 amends 10-11-320(B) Capitol grounds parking: This section does not apply to a person who possesses firearms and is authorized to park on the capitol grounds or in the parking garage below the capitol grounds.
Sec. 3 amends 16-23-20 unlawful carrying of handguns: carry is unlawful only into listed places, regardless of permit: It is unlawful, whether or not the person has a concealed weapon permit, for anyone to carry about the person any handgun, whether concealed or not, unless otherwise specifically authorized by law into a:
Sec. 4 amends 16-23-50(A)(2): penalties for violating 16-23-20 (misdemeanor, tiered by offense): A person violating the provisions of Section 16-23-20 is guilty of
Sec. 5 amends 16-23-55 found handguns: No handgun may be returned until the individual fully completes the application.
Sec. 6 amends 16-23-420 firearms on school property; Sec. 7 amends 16-23-430 school grounds: Section 16-23-420. (A) It is unlawful for a person to possess a firearm of any kind on any premises or property owned, operated, or controlled by a private or public school
Sec. 8 amends 16-23-465 alcohol premises signage; Sec. 9 amends 23-31-215(K),(M),(O),(U) permit card, lost-permit fine, lost/stolen firearm reporting: (K) A permit holder must have his permit identification card in his possession whenever he carries a concealable weapon.
Sec. 10-14 amend signage and place rules (16-23-465 etc., 51-3-? park firearm rules, residences, motorcycle saddlebag): The prohibition contained in this section does not apply to persons specified in Section 16-23-20, item (B)(1).
Sec. 15 repeals 16-23-460, 23-31-225, 23-31-230: Sections 16-23-460, 23-31-225, and 23-31-230 of the S.C. Code are repealed.
Sec. 16 amends 16-23-500 (convicted persons possessing firearms): Section 16-23-500. (A) Except as provided in subsection (F), it is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of a
Sec. 17-19 expungement general, public defenders carrying in correctional facilities, officer search/detain limits: This article does not prevent a law enforcement officer from searching, detaining, or arresting a person
Sec. 20 new 17-1-65 expungement of one conviction for unlawful handgun possession: A person may apply for an expungement of one conviction for unlawful possession of a handgun as provided in Section 16-23-20
Sec. 21 SLED permit training course, free, offered in every county: The State Law Enforcement Division shall provide a statewide concealed weapon permit training course that satisfies the proof of training requirement
Sec. 22 new 16-23-495: up to 3 years added for a concealable weapon crime without a permit; SLED notice and campaign: A person convicted of committing or attempting to commit a crime involving a concealable weapon, as defined by Section 23-31-210(5), in violation of an offense listed in Chapter 23, Title 16, or a violation of Section 10-11-320, must be imprisoned not to exceed three years.
Sec. 23 amends 23-31-215(A): permit age 21 to 18: SLED must issue a permit, which is no larger than three and one-half inches by three inches in size, to carry a concealable weapon to a resident or qualified nonresident who is at least eighteen years of age
Sec. 24-27 intent clause, savings, severability, effective date: No provision in this act should be construed as the General Assembly discouraging responsible gun ownership
